statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases to 6 after the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen printed without a gap, NQ trading 29,524.25 inside a 36-point two-sided range on light volume, while stress holds at 71 on WTI at $94.28, Brent near $99.35 and a 10-year at 4.806%.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with normal mean-reverting behaviour. The reopen flagged in the previous assessment has resolved benignly: Nasdaq-100 futures restarted without a gap and have traded a 36-point two-sided range around the pre-halt reference on light volume. That removes the horizon's nearest genuine discontinuity from the observed record, and no repeated extension after a failed retracement has been seen at any point since Tuesday's cash open. Cross-asset channels stay firm but conflicting, which sustains stress rather than tail. The flagged window now moves to Wednesday's 13:30 UTC US cash open, the next genuine liquidity discontinuity, given an active US-Iran tanker conflict, a declared Houthi blockade of Saudi Red Sea shipping and Brent near $100. Tail remains far below the block threshold across all 24 forecast hours.
headline: NQ reopens without a gap at 29,524.25 in a 36-point two-sided range, easing tail to 6, while WTI at $94.28, Brent near $99.35 and a 4.806% 10-year hold stress at 71
body:
Globex reopened at 22:00 UTC and the reopen was orderly. Nasdaq-100 futures last traded 29,524.25, down 14.50 points or 0.05% against a 29,538.75 prior close, inside a 29,503.00 to 29,539.25 range on roughly 1,800 contracts. Two independent quote sources agree on the level to within one point, so the reference is corroborated. The practical significance is that the discontinuity flagged in the previous assessment has now been observed and it produced no gap, no one-way structure and a range of only 36 points. The 21:00 to 22:00 UTC maintenance halt carried no price path at all; this hour carries a two-sided one. Both are the opposite of the structure capable of overwhelming a mean-reversion basket, which is why tail eases to 6 rather than remaining at the 9 that the previous hour's forecast assigned to this slot as conditional reopen risk.

The cash session that preceded it closed mid-range and dispersed. The Nasdaq-100 finished at 29,507.70, down 36.45 points or 0.12%, inside a 29,400.70 to 29,655.73 day range, which places the close 107 points above the session low and 148 points below the high. Index internals diverged sharply from headline weakness: the Dow closed 628.18 points lower at 52,786.07, a 1.18% decline, the S&P 500 fell 0.58% to 7,673.52 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.32% to 26,421.41, against the Nasdaq-100's 0.12%. Within the index the semiconductor complex was bid while megacaps and application software were offered. A market rotating between its own components is not a market trending, and rotation is the environment in which mean reversion works rather than fails. Tuesday's one directional episode, the cash-open downside leg that carried the assessment to a tail of 15 in the 14:00 UTC hour, was fully retraced inside the following hours.

Cross-asset channels are why stress stays in the high band at 71. WTI is quoted at $94.284, up 1.69% and at its highest in roughly six weeks, with Brent at $99.354. The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.806%, up 2.2 basis points and near the top of a 4.760 to 4.812 range, with reporting describing it as approaching two-decade highs; the 2-year sits near 4.40%. Houthi forces struck civilian and economic sites at Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran, wounding at least 73 people, and have declared a blockade of Saudi shipping through the Red Sea, the route Riyadh has relied on since the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed. That is a genuine escalation of the energy channel and it is the reason stress does not fall further. Against it, the VIX closed at 15.72, up 2.75% inside a 15.22 to 15.94 range, which is firmer on the day but absolutely low and inconsistent with a market pricing disorderly repricing. Canada's retaliatory tariffs on roughly $20 billion of US goods remain in effect with no talks reported, and rate-hike expectations for the 15-16 September FOMC meeting stand near 58%.

The flagged window moves forward to 13:30 to 14:15 UTC on Wednesday, covering the US cash open. It is the horizon's next genuine liquidity discontinuity, and Tuesday's equivalent slot is the reason it is flagged rather than any observed Wednesday structure, of which there is none. Before it, Wednesday brings the MBA mortgage print at 11:00 UTC; after it, the Apple product keynote and the US 10-year note auction pair at 17:00 UTC and the API crude inventory report lands at 20:30 UTC. Thursday carries PPI, jobless claims and Oracle results, and Friday carries CPI. Those are checkpoints, not automatic blocks: event importance and surprise magnitude are scored as stress and confidence effects until an observed price path establishes that retracements are repeatedly failing. Confidence sits at 87. Closing levels, the post-reopen futures path, VIX, the 10-year, crude in both benchmarks, index internals, the verified calendar and current reporting were all obtained and corroborated this hour. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was collected at 20:20 UTC and is 128 minutes old at this assessment, beyond the 90-minute freshness threshold, so it was treated as stale and not used as supporting evidence; the independent research above is complete without it.

lookbackSummary: Across the last 24 hours the assessment stayed inside the EA_ON band without interruption. Tail ran between 5 and 10 from Monday evening through Tuesday morning, stepped up to 15 in the 14:00 UTC slot on an observed cash-open downside leg that left NQ near the session low, then fell back through 8, 7 and 6 as that leg was fully retraced, ran at 8 through the power hour and closed the window at 5 during the maintenance halt. Stress climbed steadily from the low 60s during Monday's Labor Day holiday session to 72 in early Tuesday afternoon as crude extended on the Saudi facility strikes and Canada's retaliatory tariffs took effect, eased to the high 60s through the afternoon, and firmed back to 72 into the close as crude pressed to six-week highs. Confidence improved from 78 to 89 as the overnight evidence base was replaced by live cash-session observation, easing to 88 in the final halt hour. The dominant mode was mixed for almost the entire window because cross-asset signals kept diverging from Nasdaq price action, and turned to trend-down only for the single hour that carried the decline. The 09:00 UTC slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The horizon opens with the Globex reopen already observed and benign, so conditional tail starts at 6 rather than the 9 previously assigned to this slot. It holds at 6 through the first full hour of restored trade, lifts to 7 at the Asian cash open as Tokyo and Seoul price Tuesday's US close and the Saudi escalation for the first time, and eases back to 6 through the quiet Asian mid-session where event density is at its horizon low. Conditional tail then steps to 7 into the European pre-open and 8 at the 07:00 UTC European cash open, the horizon's first regional liquidity discontinuity, before easing to 7 through the European late morning and firming to 8 for the 11:00 UTC MBA print and the US pre-market. The horizon peak of 13 falls in the 14:00 UTC hour, the first full hour after Wednesday's US cash open, because opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the specific structure capable of overwhelming mean reversion; nothing about that structure is observed, and Tuesday's equivalent slot reached 15 before fully retracing. Scores decay through midday before lifting to 10 at the 17:00 UTC pairing of Apple's product keynote with the US 10-year note auction, hold at 9 through the afternoon and the 20:30 UTC API crude report, and close the horizon at 7 as Wednesday's maintenance halt begins. All 24 slots stay inside the EA_ON band. Three unresolved channels could force a step change in either direction: Middle East energy, where a declared Houthi blockade of Saudi Red Sea shipping now compounds an already constrained Hormuz route; the North American trade dispute after Canada's tariffs took effect with no talks under way; and rate expectations, with roughly 58% priced for a hike at the 15-16 September FOMC meeting ahead of Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI. Stress stays in the high band throughout because none of those channels resolves inside the horizon, while confidence decays overnight as the current evidence set ages and recovers once Wednesday's European and US sessions provide fresh observable structure.
